local.heading: Mount Pleasant runs 24 miles up Highway 17, and your customers search along all of it.
paragraphs: Mount Pleasant started at the Old Village, where the Hibben House on Hibben Street dates to 1755 and the Pitt Street Shops still anchor the neighborhood. Over time the town limits pushed northeast about 24 miles along U.S. 17, nearly to Awendaw. It is now the fourth-largest municipality in South Carolina, with roughly 95,600 residents, and its population doubled between 1990 and 2000. A customer in Dunes West and a customer near Patriots Point live in the same town but a long drive apart.

That length matters when someone searches on a phone. Google ranks local results partly by distance, so a contractor based near Long Point Road is not automatically in front of a homeowner in Carolina Park, up along Highway 17 near Highway 41. A website that names the parts of Mount Pleasant you cover, with a Google Business Profile that says the same thing, gives you a fair shot across the whole town instead of only the few miles around your shop.

Most of the competition here is small. Charleston Metro Chamber figures reported by Mount Pleasant Magazine in 2019 put 97% of East Cooper companies under 50 employees and 89% under 20. The bigger employers in town on that list include the Town of Mount Pleasant, East Cooper Medical Center, Mediterranean Shipping Company, Vibra Healthcare and Sandpiper Village. So the plumber, the dentist and the boutique are mostly up against businesses their own size, and the website is one of the few places a customer can tell them apart.

Mount Pleasant also gets a steady flow of visitors. Shem Creek's boardwalk and creekside seafood restaurants pull people over the Cooper River from Charleston, and the town sits on the road to Sullivan's Island and Isle of Palms. The Town is also rebuilding Coleman Boulevard between Mill Street and Pherigo Street with new stormwater, roadway and utility work. A restaurant or shop on that stretch needs its hours, menu and parking details right on the site and on Google for locals and first-timers alike.

howWeWork.heading: How we work with Mount Pleasant businesses from Villa Rica
paragraphs: We're based in Villa Rica, Georgia, west of Atlanta, and Mount Pleasant is a long drive from us. Most of the work doesn't need the drive. We start with a video call to learn how your business runs and which parts of town matter, then send you a working draft you can click through on your phone. You mark it up, we revise, and it goes live when you say it's right.

If the project calls for photos on site or a sit-down with your team, we plan a trip to the Lowcountry. The rest happens over calls, shared drafts and a short monthly report. The two people who build your site and run your SEO are the same two you talk to, from the first call through every month after launch.

faqs.q: How much does a website cost for a Mount Pleasant, SC business?
faqs.a: Most Mount Pleasant businesses start with our Local Marketing Package at $297 a month, month to month, with no contract. It includes local SEO, paid ads management if you want ads (your ad budget is separate), and a custom website valued at $3,500 at no extra cost.

faqs.q: Can my Mount Pleasant business show up in Charleston searches too?
faqs.a: Google weighs where the searcher is, so someone downtown usually sees downtown businesses first. We focus your site on Mount Pleasant and the East Cooper areas you serve, then add pages for other parts of the Charleston area only where you really take jobs.

faqs.q: Do tourists matter for my website?
faqs.a: It depends on what you sell. A Shem Creek restaurant or a shop on the way to the beaches gets plenty of first-time visitors who find it on Google Maps. A plumber in Dunes West mostly doesn't. We set up the site and your Google profile for the customers you actually get.

faqs.q: I'm in North Mount Pleasant. Will people near the bridge find me?
faqs.a: Distance is part of how Google ranks local results, so showing up far from your address takes more work. Area pages, reviews that mention those neighborhoods and a complete Google Business Profile all help. We'll tell you plainly where organic search is realistic and where ads make more sense.

faqs.q: Do we need to meet in person?
faqs.a: No. We're in Villa Rica, Georgia, and most of the work happens over video calls and shared drafts you can review on your phone. When a visit makes the project better, such as a photo day at your shop, we come to Mount Pleasant.

faqs.q: How long does a new site take to launch?
faqs.a: Usually a few weeks from the first call. Most of the timeline depends on how fast we get your photos, service details and feedback on the draft. Local SEO work starts at the same time, so the site goes live with its titles, pages and Google profile already lined up.
